desc:
The strings s and t have the same length. In one step you may pick any position of t and replace its letter by any other lowercase letter. Return the minimum number of steps needed so that t becomes an anagram of s (it contains exactly the same letters as s, in any order).

s = "friend",  t = "family"   result = 4
s = "anagram", t = "mangaar"  result = 0
s = "aab",     t = "bbb"      result = 2
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
hints: The order of the letters of t is irrelevant, only how many copies of each letter it has.
A letter that t already has in the right amount needs no change. Which letters of t are surplus, and which letters are missing?
For every letter the surplus is max(0, count_t - count_s). Each replacement turns one surplus letter into one missing letter, so the answer is the sum of all surplus values.
editorial: Let cs[c] and ct[c] be the letter counts. For each letter with ct[c] > cs[c], the extra ct[c] - cs[c] copies in t are surplus; for each letter with ct[c] < cs[c] copies are missing. Since both strings have the same length, total surplus equals total missing.

Each step can fix at most one surplus letter (changing it to a missing one), and one step per surplus letter always suffices, so the minimum is the total surplus. This takes O(n) time with two arrays of 26 counters.
